title: The recovery model centres on the potential to recover
body: The recovery model, recovery approach or psychological recovery is an approach to mental disorders or substance dependence that emphasizes and supports a person's potential for recovery.

title: Consequences that make a behaviour more likely
body: In behavioral psychology, reinforcement refers to consequences that increase the likelihood of an organism's future behavior, typically in the presence of a particular antecedent stimulus.

title: Relapse prevention identifies the high-risk situations first
body: Relapse prevention (RP) is a cognitive-behavioral approach to relapse with the goal of identifying and preventing high-risk situations such as unhealthy substance use, obsessive-compulsive behavior, sexual offending, obesity, and depression.

title: Chewing on it is not the same as solving it
body: Rumination is the sustained focus on and repetition of negative thoughts and emotions.

title: Stop at good enough, deliberately
body: Satisficing is a decision-making strategy or cognitive heuristic that entails searching through the available alternatives until an acceptability threshold is met, without necessarily maximizing any specific objective.

title: Depression that returns at the same time each year
body: Seasonal affective disorder is a mood disorder subset in which people who typically have normal mental health throughout most of the year exhibit depressive symptoms at the same time each year.

title: SSRIs are the antidepressants typically used
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are a class of drugs that are typically used as antidepressants in the treatment of major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and other psychiatric conditions.

title: Turn compassion on yourself when you fail
body: In psychology, self-compassion is extending compassion to one's self in instances of perceived inadequacy, failure, or general suffering.

title: Self-control is an executive function, not a virtue
body: Self-control is the ability to regulate one's emotions, thoughts, and behavior in the face of temptations and impulses. It is an aspect of inhibitory control, one of the core human executive functions.

title: Motivation needs autonomy, competence and relatedness
body: Self-determination theory (SDT) is a macro theory of human motivation and personality regarding individuals' innate tendencies toward growth and innate psychological needs.

title: Believing you can act changes whether you do
body: In psychology, self-efficacy is an individual's belief in their capacity to act in the ways necessary to reach specific goals. The concept was originally proposed by the psychologist Albert Bandura in 1977.

title: Self-handicapping is avoiding effort so failure does not count
body: Self-handicapping is a cognitive strategy by which people avoid effort in the hopes of keeping potential failure from hurting self-esteem.

title: Self-harm is usually without suicidal intention
body: Self-harm is intentional behavior that causes harm to oneself. This is most commonly regarded as direct injury of one's own tissues, usually without suicidal intention.

title: Self-help groups are voluntary and shared
body: Self-help groups for mental health are voluntary associations of people who share a common desire to overcome mental illness or otherwise increase their level of cognitive or emotional wellbeing.
source: Self-help groups for mental health, Wikipedia

title: Self-esteem bends how you perceive yourself
body: A self-serving bias is any cognitive or perceptual process that is distorted by the need to maintain and enhance self-esteem, or the tendency to perceive oneself in an overly favorable manner.

title: Working through the sleep period has its own disorder
body: Shift work sleep disorder (SWSD) is a circadian rhythm sleep disorder characterized by insomnia, excessive sleepiness, or both affecting people whose work hours overlap with the typical sleep period.

title: Sleep apnea is breathing that stops during sleep
body: Sleep apnea is a sleep-related breathing disorder in which repetitive pauses in breathing, periods of shallow breathing, or collapse of the upper airway during sleep result in poor ventilation and sleep disruption.

title: Lost sleep accumulates
body: Sleep debt or sleep deficit is the cumulative effect of not getting enough sleep. A large sleep debt may lead to mental or physical fatigue, and can adversely affect one's mood, energy, and ability to think clearly.

title: Short sleep is a health condition
body: Sleep deprivation, also known as sleep insufficiency or sleeplessness, is the health condition of not having adequate duration or quality of sleep to support proper alertness, performance, and health.

title: A sleep disorder is a medical disorder
body: A sleep disorder, or somnipathy, is a medical disorder that disrupts an individual's sleep patterns and quality. This can cause serious health issues and affect physical, mental, and emotional well-being.

title: Sleep responds to habits and surroundings
body: Sleep hygiene is a behavioral and environmental practice developed in the late 1970s as a method to help people with mild to moderate insomnia.

title: You are impaired right after waking
body: Sleep inertia is a physiological state of impaired cognitive and sensory-motor performance that is present immediately after awakening.

title: Sleep has its own medical specialty
body: Sleep medicine or somnology is a medical specialty or subspecialty devoted to the diagnosis and therapy of sleep disturbances and disorders.

title: Social anxiety becomes a disorder when it impairs daily life
body: Social anxiety disorder (SAD), previously known as social phobia, is an anxiety disorder characterized by high levels of anxiety and self-consciousness in social situations, resulting in significant distress and an impaired ability to function in daily life.

title: Social comparison is how you try to evaluate yourself
body: Social comparison theory, initially proposed by social psychologist Leon Festinger in 1954, centers on the belief that individuals drive to gain accurate self-evaluations.

title: Being around others can improve your performance
body: Social facilitation is a social phenomenon in which being in the presence of others improves individual task performance. That is, people do better on tasks when they are with other people rather than when they are doing the task alone.

title: Isolation is lack of contact, loneliness is how it feels
body: Social isolation is a state of complete or near-complete lack of contact between an individual and society. It differs from loneliness, which reflects temporary and involuntary lack of contact with other humans in the world.

title: You try less in a group than alone
body: In social psychology, social loafing is the phenomenon of a person exerting less effort to achieve a goal when they work in a group than when working alone.

title: Social psychology is how other people shape what you think and do
body: Social psychology is the methodical study of how thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are influenced by the actual, imagined, or implied presence of others.

title: Social support is knowing help is there
body: Social support is the perception and actuality that one is cared for, has assistance available from other people, and, most popularly, that one is part of a supportive social network.

title: SaaS is software delivered and run by the provider
body: Software as a service is a cloud computing service model in which a provider delivers application software to clients while managing the required physical and software resources.

title: Excessive focus on physical symptoms is itself a disorder
body: Somatic symptom disorder (SSD) is a mental disorder characterized by an excessive focus on physical symptoms—such as pain or shortness of breath—that cause significant distress or impairment.

title: Spread the practice out, don't cram it
body: The spacing effect demonstrates that learning is more effective when study sessions are spaced out.

title: A startup exists to find a scalable business model
body: A startup or start-up is a company or project typically undertaken by an entrepreneur to seek, develop, and validate a scalable business model.

title: The current state is the reference point for everything else
body: A status quo bias or default bias is a cognitive bias which results from a preference for the maintenance of one's existing state of affairs. The current baseline is taken as a reference point, and any change from that baseline is perceived as a loss or gain.

title: Planned procrastination has a name
body: Student syndrome refers to planned procrastination, when a student will substantially apply themselves to an assignment or task at the last moment before its deadline.

title: Subscriptions are recurring payment for continued access
body: The subscription business model is a business model in which a customer must pay a recurring price at regular intervals for access to a product or service. The model was pioneered by publishers of books and periodicals in the 17th century.

title: Persistent use despite substantial harm is the definition
body: Substance use disorder (SUD) is the persistent use of drugs despite substantial harm and adverse consequences to self and others. Related terms include substance use problems and problematic drug or alcohol use.

title: Suicidal ideation is thinking about the possibility of suicide
body: Suicidal ideation, or suicidal thoughts, is the thought process of having ideas or ruminations about the possibility of dying by suicide.

title: Suicide is often preventable
body: Suicide prevention is a collection of efforts to reduce the risk of suicide. Suicide is often preventable, and the efforts to prevent it may occur at the individual, relationship, community, and society level.

title: What you already spent is gone either way
body: In economics and business decision-making, a sunk cost is a cost that has already been incurred and cannot be recovered. Sunk costs are contrasted with prospective costs, which are future costs that may be avoided if action is taken.

title: You only see the ones that made it
body: Survivorship bias or survivor bias is a statistical error that results from concentrating on entities that passed a selection process while overlooking those that did not. This can lead to incorrect conclusions because of incomplete data.

title: Switching tasks is set-shifting, an executive function
body: Task switching, or set-shifting, is an executive function that involves the ability to subconsciously shift attention between one task and another.

title: Psychiatric care can be delivered remotely
body: Telepsychiatry or telemental health refers to the use of telecommunications technology to deliver psychiatric care remotely for people with mental health conditions. It is a branch of telemedicine.

title: Retrieving beats rereading
body: The testing effect suggests long-term memory is increased when part of the learning period is devoted to retrieving information from memory.

title: Give the activity a maximum time and stop there
body: In agile principles, timeboxing is the allocation of a maximum unit of time to an activity, called a timebox, within which a planned activity takes place. It is used by agile principles-based project management approaches and for personal time management.

title: Treatment-resistant depression means two adequate trials failed
body: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) is often defined as major depressive disorder in which an affected person does not respond adequately to at least two different antidepressant medications at an adequate dose and for an adequate duration.

title: Cycles shorter than a day run through your day
body: In chronobiology, an ultradian rhythm is a recurrent period or cycle repeated throughout a 24-hour day. In contrast, circadian rhythms complete one cycle daily, while infradian rhythms such as the menstrual cycle have periods longer than a day.

title: Gaming disorder is compulsive use that impairs life
body: Video game addiction (VGA), also known as gaming disorder or internet gaming disorder, is generally defined as a behavioural addiction involving problematic, compulsive use of video games that results in significant impairment to an individual's ability to function in various life domains over a prolonged period of time.

title: Deliberate sleep deprivation is used to treat mood disorders
body: Wake therapy is a specific application of intentional sleep deprivation. It encompasses many sleep-restricting paradigms that aim to address mood disorders with a form of non-pharmacological therapy.

title: Work-life balance is the equilibrium between the two
body: In the intersection of work and personal life, the work–life balance is the equilibrium between the two. There are many aspects of one's personal life that can intersect with work, including family, leisure, and health.

title: Working compulsively despite the damage is workaholism
body: A workaholic is a person who works compulsively. A workaholic experiences an inability to limit the amount of time they spend on work despite negative consequences such as damage to their relationships or health.

title: Working memory holds a little, briefly
body: Working memory is a cognitive system with a limited capacity that can hold information temporarily. It is important for reasoning and the guidance of decision-making and behavior.

title: Worry is distress from anticipated fear
body: Worrying is the mental distress or agitation resulting from anxiety, usually coming from a place of anticipatory fear (terror) or fear coming from a present threat (horror).

title: Writing is used clinically for healing and growth
body: Writing therapy is a form of expressive therapy that uses the act of writing and processing the written word in clinical interventions for healing and personal growth.

title: Some pressure sharpens you, more of it ruins you
body: The Yerkes–Dodson law is an empirical relationship between arousal and performance, originally developed by psychologists Robert M. Yerkes and John Dillingham Dodson and published, in 1908, in the Journal of Comparative Neurology and Psychology.

title: An unfinished task keeps talking to you
body: In psychology, the Zeigarnik effect postulates that people remember unfinished or interrupted tasks better than completed tasks.

title: Two weeks is the line
body: Seek professional help for severe or distressing symptoms that have lasted two weeks or more: trouble sleeping, appetite or weight changes, trouble concentrating, losing interest in things you enjoy, or not being able to finish your usual tasks.

title: Stress and anxiety are not the same thing
body: Stress is a response to an external cause and it goes away once the situation resolves. Anxiety is internal, persists even with no immediate threat, and interferes with how you live. The difference is what tells you when to get help.

title: Three signals that stress has gone too far
body: You may be at risk for an anxiety disorder if the symptoms of your stress interfere with everyday life, make you avoid doing things, or seem to be always present.

title: Start with a doctor, not a diagnosis
body: Talk to a primary care provider first. They can rule out a physical cause, because trouble concentrating or a change in mood is sometimes a medical condition, and refer you to a psychologist, psychiatrist or clinical social worker.

title: Talk therapy has a method
body: Psychotherapy helps you identify and change troubling emotions, thoughts and behaviours. Cognitive behavioural therapy makes you aware of automatic thinking that is inaccurate or harmful, then has you question it and see how it drives what you do.

title: Therapy and medication are both first-line
body: Psychotherapy and medication are the two main treatments for anxiety, and many people benefit from a combination of the two. Which one fits is a decision to make with a professional, not alone.

title: Everyone is distracted sometimes, ADHD is different
body: It is common to show inattention, restlessness and impulsivity now and then. In ADHD the behaviours are frequent, show up across school, work, home and relationships at once, and interfere with daily life.

title: ADHD rarely travels alone
body: ADHD often co-occurs with sleep problems, anxiety or depression, which makes all of them harder to diagnose and treat. NIH-supported research points at sleep as a target for early intervention.

title: Decide what waits, then say no
body: Set goals and priorities: decide what must get done now and what can wait, and learn to say no to new tasks when you are taking on too much. At the end of the day, count what you did finish.

title: Self-care is an input, not a reward
body: Thirty minutes of walking, regular meals and water, a sleep schedule with less screen light before bed, and one relaxing activity you actually enjoy. Small acts add up, and they support treatment rather than replace it.

title: Name the unhelpful thought, then argue with it
body: Identify and challenge your negative and unhelpful thoughts. That single move is the engine of cognitive behavioural therapy, and it works outside a therapist's office too.

title: Nobody trains themselves to need less sleep
body: A common myth is that people can learn to get by on little sleep with no negative effects. Sleep deficiency makes learning, focusing and reacting harder, and it is linked to depression, heart disease and injury.
source: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
